questions.enonce_markdown:
Give any FOUR factors that are considered when setting up a retail business.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Before opening a shop, the trader must make a careful study of several factors, because a wrong decision can lead to failure.

1. **Capital available.** The trader needs money to rent or buy premises, to buy stock, to pay staff and to meet running costs. The size and type of the business must fit the capital that can be raised.

2. **Location (site).** The shop must be in a place with many potential customers and easy access, with good roads and parking space, security and light, and near the suppliers.

3. **Type of goods and the market.** The trader decides what to sell (food, clothes, hardware) according to the needs, tastes and income of the people living in the area, and checks the size of the demand.

4. **Competition.** He studies the number of other shops selling the same goods and tries to offer something better (price, service, range of goods).

5. **Legal requirements.** A trade licence or registration may be required, and the shop must respect health, safety and tax rules.

(Other correct points: availability of suppliers and of staff, size of premises, opening hours, risks.)

**Conclusion.** A good choice of capital, place, goods and legal papers gives the retail business a good start.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline any FOUR features of a co-operative society.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** A co-operative society is an association of people who join voluntarily to help themselves and each other, for example to buy goods, sell farm products or save money, in order to obtain better terms than they could alone.

1. **Voluntary membership.** People join of their own free will and may leave when they want. Membership is open to all who accept the rules, and a minimum number of members is needed to register the society.

2. **Democratic control: one member, one vote.** Each member has one vote, whatever the number of shares he owns. Members elect a management committee which runs the society for them.

3. **Mutual help and service, not profit.** The main aim is to serve the members (lower prices, better markets, cheap loans) and not to make the greatest possible profit for a few owners.

4. **Limited interest on shares and distribution of the surplus.** Members receive only a limited rate of interest on their shares. The surplus (profit) is shared among members in proportion to their purchases or sales (a bonus or dividend) or put in reserve.

5. **Registration and legal personality.** The society is registered under the co-operative law, has a legal personality of its own, and the liability of members is normally limited to their shares.

**Conclusion.** These features distinguish a co-operative from a business run for private profit.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State any FOUR importance of warehousing to wholesalers.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Warehousing is the storing of goods in a building (warehouse) from the time they are produced or bought until they are sold. It is very important to the wholesaler for the following reasons.

1. **Storage of goods in bulk.** The wholesaler buys in large quantities from producers and can keep the goods until the retailers need them.

2. **Continuous supply.** Goods that are produced at one season (for example crops) are kept and supplied throughout the year, so retailers and consumers are served regularly.

3. **Protection of goods.** A warehouse protects the goods against theft, damage, fire, bad weather and pests, so losses are reduced.

4. **Breaking bulk, grading and packing.** Large consignments are divided into small lots, sorted, packed and labelled in the warehouse ready for the retailers.

(Other correct points: it helps to stabilise prices by controlling the quantity put on the market; goods in a bonded warehouse can be kept without paying duty until sold; a warehouse keeper's receipt can help to obtain credit.)
